prompt: Implement the 'jump to matching brace' feature every IDE has. Complete BraceMatchFinder, then run the tests.
explanation: A single depth counter is enough for one kind of bracket: start at the opening brace, add one for every '{' and subtract one for every '}', and the index where the counter returns to zero is the match. Falling out of the loop without reaching zero means the brace is never closed, which is the -1 case. isBalanced uses the same counter over the whole text, but it also has to reject a '}' that arrives while the depth is already zero -- checking only the final total would wrongly accept "}{".
hints: Validate openIndex first: it must be inside the string and the character there must be '{'.
Start the counter at 0 and begin the loop AT openIndex, so the opening brace itself bumps it to 1.
For isBalanced, returning false the moment the counter goes negative is what separates "}{" from "{}".
